contentBlocks.text: You now know five letters and two vowels! Today, one more consonant: N.

The letter N makes a humming sound: n, like at the start of 'net' or 'nap'. Try blending: /n/ /a/ /p/ — nap! And /p/ /i/ /n/ — pin! Notice N can start a word (nap) or end one (pin) — letters and sounds work the same way no matter where they show up in a word.
You now know six letters — S, M, A, T, P, I, and N — enough to read many real words! Tomorrow we'll blend a whole set of new words using everything you know.

objectives: Recognize and produce the /n/ sound for the letter N
Blend N in both starting and ending positions to read 'nap' and 'pin'
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review P and I from earlier this week.
2. Introduce N and its humming sound.
3. Blend n-a-p and p-i-n together, noticing N appears at the start of one word and the end of the other.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace N, then trace and blend both new words.
5. Close by counting all the letters learned so far: S, M, A, T, P, I, N — seven!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on N at just one position (starting sound in 'nap') before adding the ending-sound example
Ready for more: ask the child to think of one more real word with N at the start and one with N at the end
This is the first lesson to explicitly show a letter working in different word positions — a genuinely useful generalization
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and blending activity — check that the child can produce the /n/ sound and successfully blend both 'nap' and 'pin'.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: N completes a seven-letter set (S, M, A, T, P, I, N) capable of forming many real CVC words, setting up tomorrow's full blending-practice lesson.

generationData.instructions: Trace each letter, say its sound out loud, then write it once more on your own.
